summary: Three fixes, shipped as patch bumps of @cipherstash/stack-supabase and @cipherstash/stack. (1) The Supabase v3 builder now rejects a free-text needle that is empty or shorter than the ngram token_length (3 codepoints). The check sits in the term resolver that every encrypted filter term goes through (matches, like/ilike, not, or, raw cs). This closes a real fail-open: a short needle blooms to nothing, so the filter matched every row and the caller decrypted the whole table. That also applied to update/delete filtered by such a needle. The fix is fail-closed. Its release risk is that existing callers who pass short or empty search terms now get an error instead of rows, in a patch release. (2) withLockContext on the Supabase builder now accepts a plain { identityClaim } as well as a LockContext. This is a type-only widening: the value is passed unchanged to encryption operations that already accept LockContextInput and resolve it with resolveLockContext. (3) EncryptionErrorTypes is now `as const`, which narrows EncryptionError['type'] from string to a union of literals. This is compile-time only, but it can stop some TypeScript consumers compiling after the upgrade. A tsconfig paths entry affects type tests only; no src file imports that specifier. No tests were run and no CI results were available. Impact is medium. A focused review should look at the user-visible behaviour change and the patch-level type narrowing. The v2 Supabase like/ilike paths stay unguarded; that was already true at base and is not caused by this change.

behaviour_changes.description: Supabase v3 encrypted free-text terms (matches, like/ilike delegated to matches, not(col,'matches'), or() conditions, raw cs filters) whose string value is empty or has fewer codepoints than the column's ngram token_length now throw in assertTermQueryable before any encryption or PostgREST call. Previously they were encrypted to an empty bloom and matched every row.

The new rejection comes back as { data: null, error, status: 500, statusText: 'Encryption Error' }, or is rethrown under throwOnError(). It is thrown during filter encryption, which runs before the query, so a mutation with such a filter is not executed. error.encryptionError is unset because the error is a plain Error, not an EncryptionFailedError.

The withLockContext parameter on EncryptedQueryBuilderImpl and EncryptedQueryBuilderCore, and the protected lockContext field, are widened from LockContext to LockContextInput (LockContext | { identityClaim: string[] }). LockContextInput is re-exported from @cipherstash/stack-supabase. Runtime behaviour is unchanged: the value is passed as-is to encrypt/decrypt operations that already accept LockContextInput.

EncryptionErrorTypes is now `as const`. Its members, EncryptionError['type'], and the type field of each StackError member change from string to string-literal types. The runtime values are unchanged.

packages/stack/tsconfig.json maps @cipherstash/stack/errors to source, so type tests use current source instead of dist. tsup's dts build reads this tsconfig, but no packages/stack/src file imports that specifier, so build output should not change.

failure_scenarios.title: Short or empty search terms that used to return rows now return status 500 after a patch upgrade
failure_scenarios.trigger: An application on encryptedSupabaseV3 passes an empty or 1-2 character term to matches(), like('%ab%'), ilike, or(), or not(col,'matches',...). Typical sources are search-as-you-type or an empty search box treated as 'show all'.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: assertTermQueryable now calls matchNeedleError for every freeTextSearch term (query-builder-v3.ts:504-512). like/ilike strip the surrounding % and delegate to matches (844-875). or() maps matches/contains to freeTextSearch (908-916). The thrown Error is caught in execute() and returned as status 500, or rethrown under throwOnError (query-builder.ts:428-458).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Search or listing features in consumer apps that used to return results (in fact the whole table) now fail with an error after a patch-level upgrade, or throw under throwOnError. The failure is loud and fail-closed, and no data is exposed or corrupted. Callers must add their own length check. Negated not(col,'matches','ab') used to return no rows and now errors.

failure_scenarios.title: `as const` on EncryptionErrorTypes breaks compilation for some TypeScript consumers in a patch release
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer's TypeScript code compares error.type with a string outside the five literals, assigns a string-typed value to the type field of an EncryptionError-shaped object (for example in mocks or wrappers), or assigns to an EncryptionErrorTypes member.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: EncryptionError.type is typed as the value type of EncryptionErrorTypes (errors/index.ts:38). With `as const` (line 13) that type is now a union of literals instead of string, so the code above raises TS2367 (no overlap), TS2322 (string not assignable) or TS2540 (read-only).
failure_scenarios.consequence: After upgrading the patch version, affected consumer builds fail type-checking. Runtime behaviour does not change, and the fix on the consumer side is mechanical.

evidence.claim: The new block calls matchNeedleError(term.value, column.build().indexes.match) when queryType is freeTextSearch and throws a [supabase v3] Error when it returns a reason.
encryptCollectedTerms calls assertTermQueryable for every collected term before any bulkEncrypt.
like/ilike on encrypted v3 columns strip leading/trailing % and delegate to matches(), so like('%ab%') produces the needle 'ab'.
Structured or() conditions with op matches/contains map to freeTextSearch, so they reach the same guard.
matchNeedleError returns a reason for an empty string or fewer codepoints than the ngram token_length, and undefined for non-strings.
Every v3 domain with the freeTextSearch capability emits indexes.match (ngram, token_length 3), so the guard's match lookup is always present for free-text columns.
execute() encrypts filter values (step 4) before building and running the query (step 5). Any throw becomes { data: null, error, status: 500 }, or is rethrown under throwOnError.
A new test asserts matches('email','ab') yields status 500 and the guard message. It covers only the matches() spelling.
Existing unit tests cover matchNeedleError for short, empty, astral, NFD and non-string inputs.
EncryptionErrorTypes now ends with `as const`.
EncryptionError.type and each specific error's type are derived from EncryptionErrorTypes, so they narrow from string to literal types.
A new type test asserts the literal member types and exhaustive switch narrowing.
LockContextInput = LockContext | Context, and resolveLockContext handles both a plain { identityClaim } and a LockContext.
withLockContext stores the LockContextInput unchanged. It is later passed only to operation.withLockContext(...) on the encrypt and decrypt paths.
EncryptOperation.withLockContext already accepts LockContextInput. grep shows the same for decrypt, bulk and model operations.
A new type test checks that withLockContext accepts { identityClaim } and rejects an unknown key.
